items.q: Rapidly progressive renal failure most commonly turns out to be:
items.exp: RPRF → RPGN (m/c), diagnosed with biopsy; severe ATN and TMA are rare causes. (Book p749)

items.q: All of the following appear under rapidly progressive renal failure in the flowchart EXCEPT:
items.exp: RPRF: RPGN (m/c), severe ATN, TMA; nephrotic syndrome sits under normal RFT with renal disease. (Book p749)

items.q: Match each item of the hypertensive-crisis branch with its label — 1) Renal artery stenosis 2) Thrombotic microangiopathy 3) Hypertensive crisis … A) Small vessel kidney disease B) Large vessel kidney disease C) Vascular cause
items.exp: Hypertensive crisis: vascular cause; RAS = large vessel kidney disease; TMA = small vessel kidney disease. (Book p749)

items.q: Normal RFT with renal disease includes nephrotic syndrome, asymptomatic urine abnormality and:
items.exp: Normal RFT with renal disease: nephrotic syn, renal tubular acidosis type I/II, asymptomatic urine abnormality. (Book p749)

items.q: Renal artery stenosis is also known as:
opts: Renovascular HTN (RVH) / renal artery occlusion disease (RAOD)
items.exp: AKA renovascular HTN (RVH) / renal artery occlusion disease (RAOD). (Book p749)

items.q: Left untreated, renal artery stenosis can progress to:
items.exp: Can progress to CKD / ischemic nephropathy. (Book p749)

items.q: Which vessel-size statement is TRUE as per the flowchart?
opts: TMA is a small vessel kidney disease while RAS is a large vessel kidney disease
TMA is a large vessel kidney disease while RAS is a small vessel kidney disease
Both TMA and RAS are small vessel diseases
Both TMA and RAS are large vessel diseases
items.exp: RAS: large vessel kidney disease; TMA: small vessel kidney disease. (Book p749)
